title: Batman
text: Batman is Bruce Wayne, a billionaire from Gotham City who fights crime as a masked vigilante. He has no superpowers and relies on his intellect, detective skills, martial arts training and technology. Batman's real name is Bruce Wayne. Batman first appeared in Detective Comics #27 in 1939. Batman was created by artist Bob Kane and writer Bill Finger. As a child, Bruce Wayne saw his parents, Thomas and Martha Wayne, shot dead by a mugger. He swore to spend his life fighting crime. No. Batman has no superpowers. No. Batman refuses to kill and does not use guns. Batman's archenemy is the Joker. Batman is also called the Dark Knight, the Caped Crusader and the World's Greatest Detective. Batman's son is Damian Wayne, whose mother is Talia al Ghul.

title: Bruce Wayne's parents
text: Bruce Wayne's parents are Thomas Wayne, a Gotham City doctor, and Martha Wayne. They were shot dead by a mugger in front of their young son, which led him to become Batman. Batman's parents were killed by a mugger named Joe Chill. Thomas and Martha Wayne were killed in an alley later known as Crime Alley.

title: Joe Chill
text: Joe Chill is the mugger who shot Thomas and Martha Wayne in front of their son Bruce, the crime that created Batman. Joe Chill first appeared in Detective Comics #33 in 1939.

title: Alfred Pennyworth
text: Alfred Pennyworth is the Wayne family's butler, who raised Bruce Wayne after his parents were murdered. He is Batman's closest confidant and looks after Wayne Manor and the Batcave. Alfred Pennyworth first appeared in Batman #16 in 1943. Bruce Wayne was raised by his butler, Alfred Pennyworth. Batman's butler is Alfred Pennyworth.

title: Robin
text: Robin is Batman's crime-fighting partner, known as the Boy Wonder. Five characters have been Robin in the main comics: Dick Grayson, Jason Todd, Tim Drake, Stephanie Brown and Damian Wayne. Robin first appeared in Detective Comics #38 in 1940. Robin was created by Bob Kane, Bill Finger and Jerry Robinson. The first Robin was Dick Grayson. The current Robin is Damian Wayne, Batman's son. Batman's sidekick is Robin.

title: Dick Grayson
text: Dick Grayson is the first Robin, a circus acrobat whom Bruce Wayne took in after his parents were murdered. As an adult he became the hero Nightwing. Dick Grayson first appeared in Detective Comics #38 in 1940. Nightwing is Dick Grayson, the first Robin. Dick Grayson's parents, the Flying Graysons, were killed by the gangster Tony Zucco, who sabotaged their trapeze.

title: Jason Todd
text: Jason Todd is the second Robin. The Joker killed him in A Death in the Family, and he later returned from the dead as the Red Hood, an antihero who uses lethal force. Jason Todd first appeared in Batman #357 in 1983. The Red Hood is Jason Todd, the second Robin. The Joker killed Jason Todd, the second Robin.

title: Tim Drake
text: Tim Drake is the third Robin. He worked out Batman's secret identity by himself and later used the name Red Robin. Tim Drake first appeared in Batman #436 in 1989. Red Robin is Tim Drake, the third Robin.

title: Damian Wayne
text: Damian Wayne is the son of Bruce Wayne and Talia al Ghul. Raised by the League of Assassins, he became the fifth Robin. Damian Wayne first appeared as a named character in Batman #655 in 2006. Damian Wayne's mother is Talia al Ghul and his father is Bruce Wayne.

title: Stephanie Brown
text: Stephanie Brown is the vigilante Spoiler, daughter of the villain Cluemaster. She served briefly as the fourth Robin and later as Batgirl. Stephanie Brown first appeared in Detective Comics #647 in 1992.

title: Barbara Gordon
text: Barbara Gordon is the best-known Batgirl and the daughter of Commissioner James Gordon. After the Joker shot and paralyzed her in The Killing Joke, she became the computer expert Oracle. Barbara Gordon first appeared in Detective Comics #359 in 1967. Oracle is Barbara Gordon, the former Batgirl. The Joker shot and paralyzed Barbara Gordon in The Killing Joke.

title: Batgirl
text: Batgirl is a heroine who works alongside Batman. The best-known Batgirl is Barbara Gordon; Cassandra Cain and Stephanie Brown have also held the name. Batgirl's real name is usually Barbara Gordon.

title: Cassandra Cain
text: Cassandra Cain is a Batgirl and one of the best fighters in the DC Universe. She is the daughter of the assassins David Cain and Lady Shiva and was raised to read body language instead of speech. Cassandra Cain first appeared in Batman #567 in 1999.

title: Batwoman
text: Batwoman is Kate Kane, a wealthy former military cadet and a cousin of Bruce Wayne who fights crime in Gotham City. Batwoman's real name is Kate Kane. The modern Batwoman, Kate Kane, first appeared in 52 #7 in 2006.

title: James Gordon
text: James Gordon is the commissioner of the Gotham City Police Department and one of Batman's most trusted allies. He is the father of Barbara Gordon. James Gordon first appeared in Detective Comics #27 in 1939. James Gordon was created by Bill Finger and Bob Kane.

title: Lucius Fox
text: Lucius Fox is the businessman who runs Wayne Enterprises for Bruce Wayne. In many versions he also supplies Batman's equipment. Lucius Fox first appeared in Batman #307 in 1979.

title: Catwoman
text: Catwoman is Selina Kyle, a skilled cat burglar in Gotham City. She is sometimes Batman's enemy, sometimes his ally, and his most enduring love interest. Catwoman's real name is Selina Kyle. Catwoman first appeared in Batman #1 in 1940, where she was called the Cat. Catwoman was created by Bill Finger and Bob Kane.

title: Harvey Bullock
text: Harvey Bullock is a gruff detective in the Gotham City Police Department and a loyal colleague of Commissioner Gordon. Harvey Bullock first appeared in Detective Comics #441 in 1974.

title: Renee Montoya
text: Renee Montoya is a Gotham City police detective who was created for Batman: The Animated Series. In the comics she later became the faceless vigilante the Question.

title: Leslie Thompkins
text: Leslie Thompkins is a Gotham doctor and a friend of the Wayne family who comforted young Bruce after his parents' murder. She runs a free clinic and knows he is Batman.

title: Vicki Vale
text: Vicki Vale is a Gotham City journalist and photographer and one of Bruce Wayne's love interests. Vicki Vale first appeared in Batman #49 in 1948.

title: Azrael
text: Azrael is Jean-Paul Valley, an assassin trained by the Order of St. Dumas. He replaced Bruce Wayne as Batman during Knightfall after Bane broke Batman's back. Azrael's real name is Jean-Paul Valley. Azrael first appeared in Batman: Sword of Azrael #1 in 1992.

title: Huntress
text: The Huntress is Helena Bertinelli, the daughter of a murdered Gotham mob family who hunts criminals with a crossbow. The Huntress's real name is Helena Bertinelli.

title: Batwing
text: Batwing is an armored hero in Batman's circle. The first Batwing was David Zavimbe, a police officer in Africa; the second is Luke Fox, the son of Lucius Fox.

title: Duke Thomas
text: Duke Thomas is the Signal, a young Gotham hero and ally of Batman who works in daylight.

title: Ace the Bat-Hound
text: Ace the Bat-Hound is Batman's dog, a German Shepherd who helps him fight crime. Ace the Bat-Hound first appeared in Batman #92 in 1955.

title: Bat-Mite
text: Bat-Mite is a small imp from another dimension with magical powers. He idolizes Batman and causes trouble by trying to help him. Bat-Mite first appeared in Detective Comics #267 in 1959.

title: Talia al Ghul
text: Talia al Ghul is the daughter of Ra's al Ghul, a love interest of Batman and the mother of his son, Damian Wayne. Talia al Ghul first appeared in Detective Comics #411 in 1971.

title: Terry McGinnis
text: Terry McGinnis is the Batman of the future in Batman Beyond, a teenager trained by an elderly Bruce Wayne.

title: Carrie Kelley
text: Carrie Kelley is the teenage girl who becomes Robin in Frank Miller's The Dark Knight Returns.

title: Gotham City Police Department
text: The Gotham City Police Department, or GCPD, is Gotham's police force. It is led by Commissioner James Gordon and calls Batman with the Bat-Signal.

title: Joker
text: The Joker is Batman's archenemy, a criminal mastermind with chalk-white skin, green hair and a permanent grin. He has no superpowers and commits crimes for his own amusement. The Joker has no definitive real name in the main comics, and his past is deliberately left uncertain. On screen he is Jack Napier in the 1989 film Batman and Arthur Fleck in the 2019 film Joker. The Joker first appeared in Batman #1 in 1940. The Joker was created by Bill Finger, Bob Kane and Jerry Robinson. The best-known origin is that he fell into a vat of chemicals that bleached his skin and drove him insane. The Joker himself says he remembers his past differently each time. The Joker's best-known partner is Harley Quinn.

title: Harley Quinn
text: Harley Quinn is Dr. Harleen Quinzel, a psychiatrist at Arkham Asylum who fell in love with her patient, the Joker, and became his accomplice. She later left him and became an antihero. Harley Quinn's real name is Dr. Harleen Quinzel. Harley Quinn first appeared in the Batman: The Animated Series episode "Joker's Favor" in 1992. Harley Quinn was created by Paul Dini and Bruce Timm.

title: Penguin
text: The Penguin is Oswald Cobblepot, a Gotham City crime boss known for his short stature, top hat and trick umbrellas. He runs the Iceberg Lounge nightclub. The Penguin's real name is Oswald Chesterfield Cobblepot. The Penguin first appeared in Detective Comics #58 in 1941. The Penguin was created by Bob Kane and Bill Finger.

title: Riddler
text: The Riddler is Edward Nygma, a criminal genius who is compelled to leave riddles and puzzles as clues to his crimes. The Riddler's real name is Edward Nygma, also spelled Nigma. The Riddler first appeared in Detective Comics #140 in 1948. The Riddler was created by Bill Finger and Dick Sprang.

title: Two-Face
text: Two-Face is Harvey Dent, Gotham City's former district attorney. After acid scarred half his face he became a criminal who makes decisions by flipping a coin. Two-Face's real name is Harvey Dent. Two-Face first appeared in Detective Comics #66 in 1942. Two-Face was created by Bob Kane and Bill Finger. The mob boss Sal Maroni threw acid in Harvey Dent's face during a trial.

title: Bane
text: Bane is a brilliant strategist and one of Batman's strongest enemies. He uses the drug Venom to boost his strength and is known as the man who broke Batman's back. Bane first appeared in Batman: Vengeance of Bane #1 in 1993. Bane was created by Chuck Dixon, Doug Moench and Graham Nolan. Bane broke Batman's back in the Knightfall storyline.

title: Scarecrow
text: The Scarecrow is Dr. Jonathan Crane, a former psychology professor who uses a fear toxin to make his victims see their worst fears. The Scarecrow's real name is Dr. Jonathan Crane. The Scarecrow first appeared in World's Finest Comics #3 in 1941.

title: Ra's al Ghul
text: Ra's al Ghul is the centuries-old leader of the League of Assassins, who stays alive by bathing in the Lazarus Pits. He is the father of Talia al Ghul and wants Batman as his heir. Ra's al Ghul first appeared in Batman #232 in 1971. Ra's al Ghul was created by Dennis O'Neil, Neal Adams and Julius Schwartz. Ra's al Ghul is Arabic for "the Demon's Head".

title: Mr. Freeze
text: Mr. Freeze is Dr. Victor Fries, a scientist who must wear a refrigerated suit to survive and who fights with a freeze gun. He turns to crime to save his terminally ill wife, Nora. Mr. Freeze's real name is Dr. Victor Fries. Mr. Freeze first appeared in Batman #121 in 1959, under the name Mr. Zero.

title: Poison Ivy
text: Poison Ivy is Dr. Pamela Isley, a botanist who can control plants and whose touch is poisonous. She commits crimes to protect the natural world. Poison Ivy's real name is Dr. Pamela Isley. Poison Ivy first appeared in Batman #181 in 1966.

title: Killer Croc
text: Killer Croc is Waylon Jones, a criminal with a rare condition that gives him crocodile-like skin, great strength and sharp teeth. Killer Croc's real name is Waylon Jones.

title: Clayface
text: Clayface is a name used by several Batman villains whose clay-like bodies let them change shape. The first was Basil Karlo, a horror-film actor. The original Clayface's real name is Basil Karlo. Clayface first appeared in Detective Comics #40 in 1940.

title: Mad Hatter
text: The Mad Hatter is Jervis Tetch, a scientist obsessed with Alice in Wonderland who controls people's minds with devices hidden in hats. The Mad Hatter's real name is Jervis Tetch. The Mad Hatter first appeared in Batman #49 in 1948.

title: Hush
text: Hush is Dr. Thomas Elliot, a surgeon and childhood friend of Bruce Wayne who hides his face in bandages and sets out to destroy him. Hush's real name is Dr. Thomas Elliot. Hush first appeared in Batman #609 in 2003. Hush was created by Jeph Loeb and Jim Lee.

title: Black Mask
text: Black Mask is Roman Sionis, a ruthless Gotham City crime lord who wears a black skull mask. Black Mask's real name is Roman Sionis. Black Mask first appeared in Batman #386 in 1985.

title: Deathstroke
text: Deathstroke is Slade Wilson, a mercenary and assassin with enhanced strength and reflexes. He began as an enemy of the Teen Titans and often fights Batman. Deathstroke's real name is Slade Wilson. Deathstroke first appeared in The New Teen Titans #2 in 1980. Deathstroke was created by Marv Wolfman and George Pérez.

title: Court of Owls
text: The Court of Owls is a secret society of wealthy families that has controlled Gotham City for centuries. Its assassins are called Talons. The Court of Owls was created by Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo.

title: Man-Bat
text: Man-Bat is Dr. Kirk Langstrom, a scientist whose serum made from bat DNA turns him into a giant bat creature. Man-Bat's real name is Dr. Kirk Langstrom. Man-Bat first appeared in Detective Comics #400 in 1970.

title: Hugo Strange
text: Hugo Strange is a brilliant, corrupt psychiatrist and one of Batman's earliest enemies. He is one of the few villains to work out that Batman is Bruce Wayne. Hugo Strange first appeared in Detective Comics #36 in 1940.

title: Victor Zsasz
text: Victor Zsasz is a serial killer who carves a tally mark into his own skin for every person he murders. Victor Zsasz first appeared in Batman: Shadow of the Bat #1 in 1992.

title: Carmine Falcone
text: Carmine Falcone, nicknamed the Roman, is a mafia boss who ruled Gotham City's organized crime in Batman's early years.

title: Sal Maroni
text: Sal Maroni is a Gotham City mob boss, best known for throwing acid at district attorney Harvey Dent and turning him into Two-Face.

title: Firefly
text: Firefly is Garfield Lynns, a pyromaniac arsonist who wears a flying suit and carries a flamethrower. Firefly's real name is Garfield Lynns.

title: Calendar Man
text: Calendar Man is Julian Day, a criminal who plans his crimes around holidays and significant dates. Calendar Man's real name is Julian Day.

title: Professor Pyg
text: Professor Pyg is Lazlo Valentin, a deranged surgeon in a pig mask who turns his victims into mindless servants called Dollotrons. Professor Pyg was created by Grant Morrison and Andy Kubert.

title: Deadshot
text: Deadshot is Floyd Lawton, an expert marksman and hired assassin who claims he never misses. He is often a member of the Suicide Squad. Deadshot's real name is Floyd Lawton. Deadshot first appeared in Batman #59 in 1950.

title: Solomon Grundy
text: Solomon Grundy is a huge, super-strong zombie who rose from Slaughter Swamp near Gotham City. In life he was a merchant named Cyrus Gold.

title: Lady Shiva
text: Lady Shiva is one of the deadliest martial artists in the DC Universe, an assassin who is the mother of Cassandra Cain.

title: League of Assassins
text: The League of Assassins is a secret order of killers led by Ra's al Ghul. In the Dark Knight film trilogy it is called the League of Shadows.

title: Batman Who Laughs
text: The Batman Who Laughs is an evil Bruce Wayne from a dark alternate Earth who was infected by the Joker's toxin, giving him Batman's mind and the Joker's cruelty. The Batman Who Laughs was created by Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo.

title: Punchline
text: Punchline is Alexis Kaye, a college student who became the Joker's girlfriend and partner after Harley Quinn left him. Punchline first appeared in Batman #89 in 2020.

title: Ventriloquist
text: The Ventriloquist is Arnold Wesker, a meek man who commits crimes through his gangster puppet, Scarface.

title: Killer Moth
text: Killer Moth is Drury Walker, a criminal who set himself up as an anti-Batman, hiring himself out to protect other crooks.

title: Anarky
text: Anarky is Lonnie Machin, a teenage prodigy who attacks corrupt institutions in the name of anarchist ideas. Anarky was created by Alan Grant and Norm Breyfogle.

title: KGBeast
text: KGBeast is Anatoli Knyazev, a Soviet-trained assassin with a weapon in place of the hand he cut off to escape Batman.

title: Kite Man
text: Kite Man is Charles "Chuck" Brown, a minor villain who commits crimes with kites and a hang glider. His catchphrase is "Hell yeah".

title: Cluemaster
text: Cluemaster is Arthur Brown, a failed game-show host who leaves clues to his crimes. He is the father of Stephanie Brown, the hero Spoiler.

title: Tony Zucco
text: Tony Zucco is the gangster who killed Dick Grayson's parents by sabotaging their trapeze act, which led Dick to become Robin.

title: Owlman
text: Owlman is an evil counterpart of Batman from an alternate Earth, a member of the Crime Syndicate.

title: Arkham Knight
text: The Arkham Knight is the masked military commander who hunts Batman in the 2015 video game Batman: Arkham Knight. He is revealed to be Jason Todd.

title: Gotham City
text: Gotham City is the dark, crime-ridden American city that Batman protects. It is home to Wayne Manor, Arkham Asylum and the Gotham City Police Department. Batman protects Gotham City.

title: Arkham Asylum
text: Arkham Asylum is the psychiatric hospital in Gotham City where many of Batman's enemies, including the Joker, are locked up. Its inmates often escape. Arkham Asylum first appeared in Batman #258 in 1974. Batman's most dangerous enemies are held in Arkham Asylum.

title: Batcave
text: The Batcave is Batman's secret headquarters, a network of caves beneath Wayne Manor. It holds the Batcomputer, his vehicles, a crime lab and a trophy room. The Batcave is underneath Wayne Manor.

title: Wayne Manor
text: Wayne Manor is the Wayne family mansion on the outskirts of Gotham City, where Bruce Wayne lives. The Batcave lies beneath it.

title: Wayne Enterprises
text: Wayne Enterprises is the business empire Bruce Wayne inherited from his family. Its wealth and technology pay for Batman's equipment.

title: Batmobile
text: The Batmobile is Batman's car, a heavily armored vehicle packed with gadgets and weapons. Batman drives the Batmobile.

title: Batsuit
text: The Batsuit is Batman's costume: a gray and black armored suit with a cape, a cowl with pointed ears and a bat symbol on the chest. It protects him and frightens criminals.

title: Utility belt
text: The utility belt is the belt Batman wears to carry his equipment, such as Batarangs, a grapple gun, smoke pellets and forensic tools.

title: Bat-Signal
text: The Bat-Signal is a searchlight that projects a bat symbol onto the sky over Gotham City. The police use it to call Batman. The police call Batman by shining the Bat-Signal into the sky.

title: Batarang
text: The Batarang is a bat-shaped throwing weapon that Batman carries in his utility belt.

title: Batplane
text: The Batplane, also called the Batwing, is Batman's aircraft.

title: Batcomputer
text: The Batcomputer is the supercomputer in the Batcave that Batman uses to analyze evidence and track criminals.

title: Blackgate Penitentiary
text: Blackgate Penitentiary is Gotham City's prison for criminals who are not insane, unlike those sent to Arkham Asylum.

title: Lazarus Pit
text: A Lazarus Pit is a pool of chemicals that can heal injuries and bring back the dead. Ra's al Ghul uses the pits to live for centuries.

title: Iceberg Lounge
text: The Iceberg Lounge is the Gotham City nightclub owned by the Penguin, which he uses as a front for his criminal business.

title: Venom
text: Venom is the super-steroid that gives Bane his enormous strength. It is pumped into his body through tubes.

title: Detective Comics
text: Detective Comics is the comic book series in which Batman first appeared, in issue #27 in 1939. The publisher DC Comics takes its name from it.

title: Batman: Year One
text: Batman: Year One is a 1987 story by writer Frank Miller and artist David Mazzucchelli that retells Bruce Wayne's first year as Batman and James Gordon's arrival in Gotham. Batman: Year One was written by Frank Miller and drawn by David Mazzucchelli.

title: The Killing Joke
text: The Killing Joke is a 1988 graphic novel by writer Alan Moore and artist Brian Bolland. The Joker shoots and paralyzes Barbara Gordon to try to drive her father insane, and the book gives a possible origin for the Joker. The Killing Joke was written by Alan Moore and drawn by Brian Bolland.

title: The Dark Knight Returns
text: The Dark Knight Returns is a 1986 comic by Frank Miller in which a 55-year-old Bruce Wayne comes out of retirement to be Batman again. The Dark Knight Returns was written and drawn by Frank Miller.

title: Knightfall
text: Knightfall is a 1993 to 1994 storyline in which Bane breaks Batman's back and Jean-Paul Valley, Azrael, takes over as a more violent Batman until Bruce Wayne returns.

title: The Long Halloween
text: The Long Halloween is a 1996 to 1997 series by writer Jeph Loeb and artist Tim Sale. Batman hunts Holiday, a killer who strikes on holidays, and Harvey Dent becomes Two-Face. The Long Halloween was written by Jeph Loeb and drawn by Tim Sale.

title: Batman: Hush
text: Batman: Hush is a 2002 to 2003 storyline by writer Jeph Loeb and artist Jim Lee in which a mysterious bandaged enemy turns Batman's foes against him.

title: A Death in the Family
text: A Death in the Family is a 1988 storyline in which the Joker kills Jason Todd, the second Robin. Readers decided his fate by telephone vote.
aliases: batman: a death in the family

title: No Man's Land
text: No Man's Land is a 1999 storyline in which Gotham City is wrecked by an earthquake, abandoned by the United States government and carved up by gangs and villains.

title: Under the Hood
text: Under the Hood is a 2005 storyline by writer Judd Winick in which Jason Todd, the Robin killed by the Joker, returns as the Red Hood.

title: Batman R.I.P.
text: Batman R.I.P. is a 2008 storyline by writer Grant Morrison in which the Black Glove, led by Dr. Simon Hurt, tries to destroy Batman's mind.

title: Batman: Three Jokers
text: Batman: Three Jokers is a 2020 series by writer Geoff Johns and artist Jason Fabok built on the idea that three different men have been the Joker.

title: Arkham Asylum: A Serious House on Serious Earth
text: Arkham Asylum: A Serious House on Serious Earth is a 1989 graphic novel by writer Grant Morrison and artist Dave McKean in which Batman enters the asylum after its inmates take it over.

title: Batman (1989 film)
text: Batman is a 1989 film directed by Tim Burton, starring Michael Keaton as Batman and Jack Nicholson as the Joker.

title: Batman Returns
text: Batman Returns is a 1992 film directed by Tim Burton, with Michael Keaton as Batman, Danny DeVito as the Penguin and Michelle Pfeiffer as Catwoman.

title: Batman Forever
text: Batman Forever is a 1995 film directed by Joel Schumacher, with Val Kilmer as Batman, Tommy Lee Jones as Two-Face and Jim Carrey as the Riddler.

title: Batman & Robin (film)
text: Batman & Robin is a 1997 film directed by Joel Schumacher, with George Clooney as Batman, Arnold Schwarzenegger as Mr. Freeze and Uma Thurman as Poison Ivy.

title: Batman Begins
text: Batman Begins is a 2005 film directed by Christopher Nolan, starring Christian Bale as Batman. It tells his origin and pits him against Ra's al Ghul and the Scarecrow.

title: The Dark Knight
text: The Dark Knight is a 2008 film directed by Christopher Nolan, with Christian Bale as Batman and Heath Ledger as the Joker. Ledger won a posthumous Academy Award for the role. Heath Ledger played the Joker in The Dark Knight.

title: The Dark Knight Rises
text: The Dark Knight Rises is a 2012 film directed by Christopher Nolan, the last of his trilogy, with Christian Bale as Batman, Tom Hardy as Bane and Anne Hathaway as Selina Kyle.

title: The Batman (film)
text: The Batman is a 2022 film directed by Matt Reeves, starring Robert Pattinson as Batman, with Paul Dano as the Riddler, Zoë Kravitz as Selina Kyle and Colin Farrell as the Penguin.

title: Joker (2019 film)
text: Joker is a 2019 film directed by Todd Phillips, starring Joaquin Phoenix as Arthur Fleck, a failed comedian who becomes the Joker. Phoenix won the Academy Award for Best Actor.

title: 1966 Batman TV series
text: Batman is a television series that ran from 1966 to 1968, starring Adam West as Batman and Burt Ward as Robin. It is known for its campy, comic tone.

title: Batman: The Animated Series
text: Batman: The Animated Series is a television cartoon that ran from 1992 to 1995, developed by Bruce Timm and Eric Radomski. Kevin Conroy voiced Batman and Mark Hamill voiced the Joker, and it introduced Harley Quinn. Kevin Conroy voiced Batman in Batman: The Animated Series. Mark Hamill voiced the Joker in Batman: The Animated Series.

title: Batman Beyond
text: Batman Beyond is an animated series that ran from 1999 to 2001. In a future Gotham, an elderly Bruce Wayne trains teenager Terry McGinnis as the new Batman.

title: Gotham (TV series)
text: Gotham is a television series that ran from 2014 to 2019 about a young James Gordon and a teenage Bruce Wayne in the years before Batman.

title: The Penguin (TV series)
text: The Penguin is a 2024 television series, a spin-off of the film The Batman, starring Colin Farrell as Oz Cobb.

title: The Lego Batman Movie
text: The Lego Batman Movie is a 2017 animated comedy film in which Will Arnett voices Batman.

title: Batman: Arkham Asylum
text: Batman: Arkham Asylum is a 2009 video game developed by Rocksteady Studios in which Batman is trapped in the asylum after the Joker takes it over. It began the Batman: Arkham series.

title: Batman: Arkham City
text: Batman: Arkham City is a 2011 video game by Rocksteady Studios, the sequel to Arkham Asylum, set in a walled-off prison district of Gotham City.

title: Batman: Arkham Knight
text: Batman: Arkham Knight is a 2015 video game by Rocksteady Studios in which Batman faces the Scarecrow and the mysterious Arkham Knight.

title: Batman: Mask of the Phantasm
text: Batman: Mask of the Phantasm is a 1993 animated film based on Batman: The Animated Series, in which Batman is blamed for murders committed by a masked killer called the Phantasm.

title: Bob Kane
text: Bob Kane was the American comic book artist who created Batman with writer Bill Finger in 1939.

title: Bill Finger
text: Bill Finger was the writer who created Batman with Bob Kane and shaped much of the character, including the costume, the Bruce Wayne identity and Gotham City. DC Comics only began crediting him in 2015.

title: Kevin Conroy
text: Kevin Conroy was the actor best known as the voice of Batman, starting with Batman: The Animated Series in 1992 and continuing in the Arkham video games.

title: Mark Hamill
text: Mark Hamill is the actor who has voiced the Joker since Batman: The Animated Series in 1992, including in the Arkham video games.

title: Frank Miller
text: Frank Miller is the writer and artist behind The Dark Knight Returns and Batman: Year One, which made Batman darker in the 1980s.

title: Christopher Nolan
text: Christopher Nolan is the director of the Dark Knight trilogy: Batman Begins, The Dark Knight and The Dark Knight Rises.

title: Batman's main villains
text:
There is no official ranking, but Batman's most prominent villains are:
1. The Joker, his archenemy.
2. Two-Face, former district attorney Harvey Dent.
3. The Penguin, crime boss Oswald Cobblepot.
4. The Riddler, Edward Nygma.
5. Bane, who broke Batman's back.
Others include Catwoman, the Scarecrow, Ra's al Ghul, Mr. Freeze, Poison Ivy and Harley Quinn.
